newsitem.title: UK: Empire Stores hits record 17 mln-stg profit in '96.
newsitem.headline: Empire Stores hits record 17 mln-stg profit in '96.

text.p: British home shopping group Empire Stores plc on Monday reported record 17 million stg operating profit in 1996, up nearly 35 percent from 1995.
Empire, one of Britain's five largest home shopping concerns, also reported record sales of 300 million stg, up 20 percent from the year earlier.
The parent of Empire is French catalogue retailer La Redoute, part of retail giant Pinault Printemps Redoute.
Empire said sales through its catalogue aimed at its traditional markets of "customers on lower incomes" achieved sales growth of nine percent.
It credited "an enhanced product offer coupled with improved marketing" with resulting in higher sales per customer.

In 1995, Empire Group launched its English language La Redoute catalogue pitched at more affluent customers. La Redoute achieved sales of 32 million stg in its first full year of operations and Empire said it was "confident of creating a significant business in the medium term."

Empire Group Managing Director Mike Hawker said the company would continue to grow and that the launch of its Vert Baudet catalogue of children's clothing and maternity wear has been "very encouraging."
